root_cause.text: The NFSv4 compound argument decode path incorrectly left `RQ_USEDEFERRAL` enabled during idmap-triggered cache lookups, allowing `cache_check()`/`svc_defer()` to set `RQ_DROPME` and drop a v4 request before response encoding and session slot cleanup.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `clear_bit(RQ_USEDEFERRAL, &rqstp->rq_flags);` in `nfs4svc_decode_compoundargs()` with comments that NFSv4 decoders can trigger cache lookups leading to `svc_defer()` and `RQ_DROPME`, and the CVE/commit message states this prevents `nfs4svc_encode_compoundres()` from running so `NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE` is never cleared.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add documentation and a one-time warning guard to catch invalid deferred-request context before performing NFSd name-to-UID idmap lookup.
intent_record.what: The function definition of nfsd_map_name_to_uid was reformatted onto a single declaration line, a kernel-doc comment block describing the function, parameters, and return value was added immediately above it, and a new comment plus a WARN_ON_ONCE(test_bit(RQ_USEDEFERRAL, &rqstp->rq_flags)); assertion were inserted before the existing name/null length validation logic.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the new WARN_ON_ONCE emits a one-time warning if nfsd_map_name_to_uid is called while the request has RQ_USEDEFERRAL set, helping detect an invalid call context where the idmap upcall could lead cache_check() to defer or drop the request and interfere with NFSv4/NFSv4.1 processing; otherwise behavior is unchanged.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a one-time warning guard in nfsd_map_name_to_gid to catch invalid deferred-request state before idmap upcalls, while documenting the function and the constraint.
intent_record.what: The function definition for nfsd_map_name_to_gid was reformatted onto a single documented declaration, a kernel-doc comment block describing the function and its parameters was added above it, and a new WARN_ON_ONCE(test_bit(RQ_USEDEFERRAL, &rqstp->rq_flags)); check with an explanatory comment was inserted before the existing input validation.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the added WARN_ON_ONCE emits a one-time warning if nfsd_map_name_to_gid is called while RQ_USEDEFERRAL is set on the request, highlighting an invalid state before the idmap lookup path that can trigger cache deferral and request dropping. It does not change normal successful execution directly, but helps detect and prevent improper use that could cause NFSv4 requests to be dropped or session slot processing to be skipped.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop re-enabling RPC deferral at the end of nfsd4 compound processing to avoid incorrect deferred-request handling.
intent_record.what: Two lines were removed from nfsd4_proc_compound() at the out: path: a comment about resetting the deferral mechanism for RPC deferrals and the call to set_bit(RQ_USEDEFERRAL, &rqstp->rq_flags); after assigning cstate->status = status.
intent_record.how: The function no longer re-enables the RQ_USEDEFERRAL flag when exiting, so this request path stops resetting or activating the RPC deferral mechanism at the end of compound processing, changing later handling of deferred RPC behavior for the request.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable deferral during NFSv4 compound argument decoding to prevent deferred compound replay issues and NFSv4.1 session slot leaks.
intent_record.what: A new comment block was added in nfs4svc_decode_compoundargs() explaining problems caused by deferral during NFSv4 compound decode, followed by a new statement clear_bit(RQ_USEDEFERRAL, &rqstp->rq_flags); inserted before the call to nfsd4_decode_compound(args).
intent_record.how: This disables request deferral for this compound decode path by clearing the RQ_USEDEFERRAL flag before operation decoding begins, preventing decoders from triggering svc_defer() and setting RQ_DROPME. At runtime, this avoids replay of deferred compound requests and prevents NFSv4.1+ session slots from being left permanently marked in use when a request is dropped after SEQUENCE succeeds.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets the bad deferred-request state around idmap upcalls—the same condition caused by leaving RQ_USEDEFERRAL enabled in the decode path. Even though it adds a warning/documentation rather than the primary fix, it is specifically about detecting and constraining the vulnerable state tied to request deferral and dropping.

The changes directly target the root cause: they disable/restrict RPC deferral during NFSv4 compound decoding/processing so idmap/cache lookup deferrals cannot mark requests for drop before reply encoding and session slot cleanup.

The added warning guard specifically checks for an invalid deferred-request context during NFSd idmap lookup, which is the same area implicated by the root cause: deferral remaining enabled during idmap-triggered cache lookups and causing requests to be dropped improperly.

candidates.rationale: This explicitly re-enabled RPC deferral at the end of NFSv4 compound processing, leaving RQ_USEDEFERRAL set during later idmap-triggered cache lookups and enabling the erroneous cache_check()/svc_defer() path that could mark the request RQ_DROPME.

The vulnerability occurs in the NFSv4 compound argument decode path because decoding proceeded without first disabling request deferral; this call enters the vulnerable decode flow where idmap lookups could occur while RQ_USEDEFERRAL remained enabled.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement re-enabled RPC deferral for the request, leaving RQ_USEDEFERRAL set across later NFSv4 processing. During subsequent idmap-triggered cache lookups, that allowed cache_check()/svc_defer() to mark the request for dropping, causing the request to be discarded before response encoding and session slot cleanup.

This statement entered the NFSv4 compound decode path without first disabling request deferral. As a result, idmap-related cache lookups during decode could run while RQ_USEDEFERRAL was still enabled, triggering the erroneous deferred-request/drop path described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body contains the relevant deferral logic directly. The root cause is that NFSv4 compound decode/processing left request deferral enabled during cases such as idmap-triggered cache lookups, allowing a cache miss to result in request drop behavior. In this commit, `nfsd4_proc_compound()` explicitly disables the deferral mechanism for non-v4.0 compounds: `rqstp->rq_usedeferral = (args->minorversion == 0);` with the comment `/* Use the deferral mechanism only for NFSv4.0 compounds */`. That means for NFSv4.1 (`minorversion != 0`), deferral is turned off during compound processing, which addresses the vulnerable condition. The function also handles the drop case when deferral is disabled: `if (!rqstp->rq_usedeferral && status == nfserr_dropit) { ... status = nfserr_jukebox; }`, converting the would-be drop into `NFS4ERR_DELAY` (`nfserr_jukebox`) instead of allowing the request to be dropped. Finally, it restores normal RPC deferral behavior afterward with `rqstp->rq_usedeferral = 1;`. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present in this version, and the fix is present.
